Reason: The recurrent, non-resolving retrocardiac opacity seen in Figures 1 and 3 (with clearance in Figure 2) is characteristic of an intralobar pulmonary sequestration, which presents as a persistent mass-like density in the left lower lobe that frequently becomes secondarily infected and temporarily clears with antibiotics before recurring.
